title: The Smallest Team That Knows Every Skill

concept.title: Take the first skill nobody covers yet and try only people who have it
body: A project needs `s` skills and there are `p` people, each with some of the skills. Find the smallest team that together has **all** the skills. Each person is a bit mask of skills, and the team so far is the OR of its members' masks (`covered`). This is the *set cover* problem: no fast general method is known, but a clever search is enough for small sizes.

The key idea: look at the **first skill that is not covered yet**. Some member of the final team **must** have it, so it is enough to try, as the next member, each person who has this skill. We never try a person who cannot help with this skill, and the order in which members are added does not matter, so no team is built twice in different orders.

The line `size + 1 >= best[0]` is a **bound**: if a team of `size` people is still incomplete, it needs at least one more member, so it cannot be smaller than `best`. Together with the rule "branch on an uncovered skill" this keeps the search tiny for 12 skills and 20 people.

statement: A project needs `s` skills, numbered 1 to `s`. There are `p` people. Each person is described by a string of `s` characters: character `i` is `1` if the person has skill `i`, and `0` otherwise. Every skill is known by at least one person. Print the smallest number of people whose skills together cover all `s` skills.
inputFormat: Each of the next `p` lines has the string of one person.
outputFormat: Print the size of the smallest team.
constraints: Every skill is known by at least one person.

examples.note: The first two people together know all four skills: the team size is 2.

hints: Store the skills of a person as a bit mask and the team as the OR of the masks.
Branch on the first skill that nobody in the team has: the next member must have it.
Keep the size of the best team found; stop a branch that cannot be smaller than it.

starter.python:
s, p = map(int, input().split())
people = [input().strip() for _ in range(p)]

# Your code here

explanation: The skills of a team are a bit mask. The search takes the lowest skill not yet covered and tries only the people who have it as the next member; a branch whose size plus one cannot beat the best team is cut.
solution.complexity: Time exponential in the worst case but small here, space O(s).

code.python:
def search(covered, size, full, by_skill, best):
    if covered == full:
        best[0] = min(best[0], size)
        return
    if size + 1 >= best[0]:
        return
    skill = (~covered & (covered + 1)).bit_length() - 1
    for mask in by_skill[skill]:
        search(covered | mask, size + 1, full, by_skill, best)

s, p = map(int, input().split())
people = [input().strip() for _ in range(p)]

masks = [sum(1 << i for i, ch in enumerate(row) if ch == "1") for row in people]
by_skill = [[m for m in masks if m >> i & 1] for i in range(s)]
best = [p + 1]
search(0, 0, (1 << s) - 1, by_skill, best)
print(best[0])
